items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 1 at 3:09PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
A frontal system continues to lift a plume of moisture into
Prince William Sound and along the coastal mountains through
Saturday morning. The heaviest precipitation, in the form of wet
snow, will fall tonight through early Saturday morning through
Thompson Pass. 7 to 12 inches of snow is possible through Saturday
morning. Southeasterly winds may gust up to 30 mph at times

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued May 1 at 2:57PM AKDT until May 2 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Sustained southerly winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 45
mph expected.

* WHERE...Municipality of Skagway.

* WHEN...From 7 AM to 1 PM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds could blow around unsecured objects. Use
extra caution if traveling by land, sea, or air.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Stronger southerly winds could arrive
earlier Saturday morning. Stay tuned to weather.gov/ajk for
updates.
items.instruction:
Use extra caution when driving, especially if operating a high
profile vehicle. Secure outdoor objects.

items.headline: High Wind Warning issued May 1 at 1:12PM AKDT until May 2 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 40 to 50 mph with gusts up to 80 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds could blow down trees and power lines.
Isolated power outages are possible. Travel could be very
difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.
items.areas: Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving very difficult, especially for
high profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued May 1 at 12:24PM AKDT until May 1 at 11:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations OF 2 TO 5 inches.
Winds gusting up to 50 mph.

* WHERE...Portage and Turnagain Pass.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Sudden changes from rain to snow will be possible
through the rest of today. Drops in visibilities reduced to one
half mile is possible due to heavy snowfall and strong winds. The
strongest wind gusts will be near Portage. Travel could be very
difficult with slick roads and rapid changes to conditions.
items.instruction:

conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

items.headline: Blizzard Warning issued May 1 at 11:48AM AKDT until May 1 at 7:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to
two inches. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Point Lay.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel may be impacted.
items.instruction:
Travel should be restricted to emergencies only. If you must travel,
have a winter survival kit with you. If you get stranded, stay with
your vehicle.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 1 at 5:18AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
A frontal system will lift a plume of moisture from the tropical
Pacific into Prince William Sound and along the coastal mountains

in the form of heavy wet snow through Thompson Pass as
temperatures range from 29 to 33 degrees. 7 to 12 inches of snow
is possible Friday morning through Saturday morning with the

items.headline: Avalanche Warning issued April 30 at 4:47PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
SABAFC

The following message is transmitted at the request of the
Chugach National Forest Avalanche Center.

...THE CHUGACH NATIONAL FOREST AVALANCHE INFORMATION CENTER HAS
ISSUED AN AVALANCHE WARNING FOR: CHUGACH STATE PARK, GIRDWOOD,
PORTAGE, TURNAGAIN PASS, INTERIOR KENAI PENINSULA, AND THE
SOUTHERN KENAI MOUNTAINS FROM 6 AM FRIDAY, MAY 1 to 6 AM SUNDAY,
MAY 3...

* WHAT...The backcountry avalanche danger is HIGH. Very dangerous
avalanche conditions exist.
